text:
maria: Quick heads-up — ran a quantization sweep for gpt-small on A100 (same SKU) across AWS/GCP/Azure. Seeing ~6% pplx regression on Azure when using TRT int8 kernels. Anyone seen this before?

aj: Can you paste the exact driver / cuda / runtime stacks and the quant config? :eyes:

maria: model: gpt-small-v1
q-config: per_channel symmetric, KL calibration 1k samples
torch=2.2, ort=1.16, cuda-driver: AWS 525.105 / GCP 525.105 / AZURE 530.30
cudnn: AWS/GCP 8.2.1, AZURE 8.3.2
trt: 8.6 vs 8.4 on azure (packaged by vendor)

sloan: Hm — we recently hit kernel fallback on AZ where some int8 GEMM variants fell back to fp16/FP32 because the PTX kernels didn't match. Check dmesg and cuobjdump for missing cubin sections. :thinking_face:

maria: here's the profile snippet I captured (trimmed):
```
[2026-04-12 14:03:21] kernel: int8_gemm_v0 launched -> returned FALLBACK_FP16
[2026-04-12 14:03:21] kernel: fallback path -> cudnn_convolution_fp16
[2026-04-12 14:03:21] perf: token/s (batch=8): 1600
```

perf-bot: autotest-summary: throughput AWS=2100 tok/s, GCP=2080 tok/s, AZURE=1600 tok/s; p95 lat AWS=28ms GCP=29ms AZURE=42ms. note: AZ run used driver 530.30 and trt 8.4 (vendor build).

liam: Could be a driver+vendor user-space mismatch rather than hardware. Same A100 SKU but different microcode/firmware + packaged libs can change PTX->cubin paths. Can you run `nvidia-bug-report.sh` and `cuobjdump --dump-sass` on the offending binary?

maria: will run. also going to try: TF_CUDNN_USE_AUTOTUNE=0 and ORT_TENSORRT_FP16_ALLOW_CUDA_FALLBACK=1 and pin cudatoolkit 11.8 vs 12.1 to see effect.

aj: Also try installing driver 530 on AWS/GCP (if feasible) to reproduce; if 530 on AWS still fine, then it's vendor trt packaging. If 530 reproduces issue across clouds -> kernel regression.

sloan: If we confirm vendor packaging is root cause, workaround options: force different GEMM kernel (`--use-kernel=gemm_fallback`), or use per-channel bias-correction quant profile to reduce sensitivity (will cost some quality). We'll add a gating rule for model onboarding tests.

maria: kicked off 3 jobs: aws-525, gcp-525, az-530 -> also job to run aws/gcp with driver 530 to isolate.

perf-bot: job 1865440500 completed: azure run with driver 530 + vendor libs (re-run) -> throughput 2050 tok/s, p95 30ms, pplx delta now ~1.2% vs fp32.

aj: That's a strong signal driver mismatch + packaging variant. We should add a cross-cloud quant check during onboarding (capture pplx delta + fallback kernel flags).

maria: created INF-904 to pin driver/quant-kernel matrix for Dedicated and to add a cross-cloud eval step in model-onboarding. attaching nsys trace link in the ticket. :thumbsup:

sloan: Thanks — once INF-904 has repro steps, Eng-Infra can add a node image test to catch this before release.

liam: Quick note for sizing: because AZ exhibited fallback we saw a ~25% throughput hit. For capacity planning, assume worst-case fallback margin until driver matrix is certified.

maria: will paste nsys flame next. cheers.
